title: Assistive admin macros and permissioned playlet registry
creator: Samira Chowdhury
description: Build a lightweight registry and runtime for small, opinionated admin macros ("playlets") that operators can run from the Console, CLI, and the new operator-assistant. Playlets are single-purpose, auditable snippets that encapsulate common admin tasks (rotate key, snapshot-and-verify, cache-warm, safedb-export). The registry enforces RBAC, parameter schemas, dry-run and idempotency guarantees, and automatic instrumentation for billing/telemetry. This work ties together runbooks-as-tasks (so runbooks can reference playlets), improves on-call ergonomics, and reduces blast radius for frequently executed support actions.
acceptance_criteria: Registry service that can register/unregister playlets with metadata and param schema
Playlet runtime supports: dry-run mode, idempotency token, and structured exit codes
RBAC checks integrated with SSO groups; unauthorized invocations are rejected and logged
Console UI surface to search/play/read docs and run playlets with preview/dry-run
CLI shim 'rwd-admin playlet run' that mirrors Console behavior and logs to audit stream
Audit trail stored in existing audit-log bucket and surfaced in Console with links to traces
Automated unit + e2e tests that simulate high-frequency invocation and failure recovery
Telemetry events emitted with standard labels (playlet_id, outcome, latency, user, caller_context)
checklist: Design API contract for registry (POST /playlets, GET /playlets/:id)
Define playlet manifest format (metadata, param schema, required-secrets, safety-rails)
Prototype dry-run semantics and idempotency token handling in the runtime
Implement RBAC middleware integrating with SAML groups and project roles
Wire audit & telemetry (log link, Datadog events, trace spans)
Console: add Run modal with parameter validation and dry-run toggle
CLI: add invocation shim + --dry-run and --auth-method flags
Integration tests: permission matrix, concurrency replay, and rollback scenarios
Run a safety review with Security & SRE, incorporate feedback
notes: Trade-offs: allowing arbitrary code in playlets increases expressivity but raises security risk; mitigate by requiring containerized sandboxing + least-privilege secrets and review process
Prefer declarative manifests (YAML) for playlet definition to enable static validation and discoverability
Consider attaching a small preflight probe that validates network/API access before a live run
Idempotency semantics: require consumer to supply idempotency key for state-mutating operations; runtime will store short-lived markers in DynamoDB
Telemetry and SLO: instrument the runtime to tag latency percentiles and error-class to feed Ops dashboards

risks: Playlets could be used to exfiltrate secrets if runtime permissions are misconfigured
High-frequency invocations might stress downstream services (DB/export) if rate limits aren't enforced
Migration: many ad-hoc admin scripts will need to be audited and ported to the manifest format
